scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
Two things on your desk collide in the next six months, and the migration is how they stop competing for the same dollars. Your $1,850,000 annual technology run-rate is structurally locked into hardware refresh cycles, Hyper-V host licensing, and SQL Server Enterprise edition across 28 instances — costs that rise on a schedule you do not control and cannot be cut without cutting capacity. Moving the load-matching tier to Google Compute Engine and the settlement data layer to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL converts that fixed obligation into consumption you can meter, right-size, and commit against, with the SQL Server licensing line retired outright as the settlement databases move to PostgreSQL. Equally important for the audit opening in six months: carrier-settlement records and driver-hours data currently live across 620 virtual machines with inconsistent backup verification and no unified audit log. The first year of this programme front-loads the settlement systems specifically because centralised, immutable logging and point-in-time recovery in Cloud SQL turn DOT evidence production from a manual reconstruction exercise into a query.

What you should expect, stated plainly: this is a $4,200,000 investment over two years against a $1,850,000 annual run-rate, and it will not pay for itself inside the audit window. Expect run-rate to rise modestly in months 1–9 while both environments operate in parallel — that dual-running cost is real and is already inside the $4,200,000. Savings begin at the first decommissioning wave and compound as the Hyper-V estate retires; we project run-rate reduction reaching a meaningful share of current spend by the end of year two, with the SQL Server licensing retirement the single largest and most certain component. The audit does not depend on programme completion — we will have settlement data and its audit trail migrated and evidence-ready ahead of the opening, which is the scope commitment we are willing to be held to. The work carrying genuine risk is the SQL Server to PostgreSQL conversion in settlement, where stored-procedure logic must be rewritten rather than lifted; we recommend a paid discovery in the first 60 days to size that precisely before you commit the full programme budget, and we would rather revise the number then than defend it later.
